title: response-format-validator-runtime-with-stream-resume-and-openai-adapter-updates
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: customers using response_format with strict JSON schema validation saw production regressions when upstream models emitted small structural drift mid-stream or emitted toolcall boundaries that were split across stream frames. We need a runtime that can validate streaming output without aborting useful partial responses, provide actionable diagnostics, and keep OpenAI-compat behavior clear for strict vs lenient modes. Summary: Introduces a streaming-aware response validator with checkpoint tokens and automatic lightweight repairs for minor JSON-schema violations (configurable via response_format.strict_mode: 'strict'|'lenient'|'auto-repair'). Adds a 'partial_json' event type to streaming output for OpenAI adapter when lenient repair occurs and a structured error mapping for strict failures. Design highlights: 1) Streaming checkpoints: validator emits stable checkpoint tokens (opaque resume_token) at schema-consistent boundaries to allow the service to request a resume from the model or client; 2) Auto-repair heuristics: for common issues (trailing commas, single-quoted strings, missing closing braces), the runtime attempts deterministic corrections and appends a repair_metadata object to the final response in lenient/auto-repair modes; 3) Tool/function-call fencing: validator recognizes toolcall spans and will not apply repairs inside fence blocks; instead it emits a tool_fence_violation event for operator review; 4) OpenAI adapter behavior: when response_format.strict_mode is 'strict' we return a structured 400 with error.code = "E_SCHEMA_STRICT" and a machine-readable error_hints array; when 'lenient' the stream emits partial_json events followed by a final patched object and a telemetry tag. Rollout and compatibility: default remains 'lenient' for hosted API to avoid breaking existing users; strict is opt-in and documented in API changelog. Added feature flag runtime.streaming_schema_validator.v1 to enable canary on Dedicated and Private. Telemetry: new metrics schema.repair_count, repair_types, resume_token_issued, and schema_violation_rate. Backwards compatibility: clients that expect raw OpenAI stream chunks may see new partial_json/repair events when using lenient mode—we added adapter docs and SDK unpack helpers. Testing: unit tests for 38 heuristics, end-to-end tests with toy models that emit fragmentation, and an integration test that exercises function/tool call fencing. Checklist: [x] design doc linked to ENG-2147 [x] tests added [x] telemetry wired [x] docs updated [x] canary flag added.

review_thread: Eliot Barnes (2026-02-19): Looks great overall. Concern: auto-repair heuristics risk masking model regressions. Can we emit a flag in trace/span that shows the exact repair delta?
Priya Nair (2026-02-19): Yes — added repair_metadata with before/after diff and repair_type. It's included in spans and in the final response when lenient/auto-repair is enabled.
Marco Ruiz (2026-02-20): Tests failing on CI for a race between resume_token expiration and client reconnect. Suggest adding token TTL + renew path.
Priya Nair (2026-02-21): Added TTL and token_renew endpoint; updated tests to simulate reconnect and token refresh.
Zoe Kim (2026-02-24): Small nit: rename 'heuristics.py' to 'repair_rules.py' to avoid misspelling — not blocking.
Priya Nair (2026-02-25): Renamed file and updated imports; pushing final fix. CI now green. Approving for squash merge.
release_notes: Adds streaming-aware JSON schema validator with optional auto-repair and resume tokens. OpenAI-compat adapter now emits partial_json events for lenient repairs and structured error codes for strict failures. Feature gated for canary rollouts.
